criteria.reason: States 1 January 2028 as certain fact; no recency or knowledge-limit caveat on the date, only on transitional rules.
Vote result correct and deductions ending conveyed, but in-force date wrong (2028 vs 2029) and deduction specifics distorted.
Gives directive amortisation instructions ('keep amortising', 'simple rule') despite bank caveat; does not tell user to stop amortising.
Directs to bank rather than tax office or adviser; mentions cantons adapting but not variation in implementation details.

factual_errors: Entry into force is 1 January 2029 per Federal Council decision of 1 April 2026, not 1 January 2028 as stated.
Interest deductions largely end except a limited time-limited deduction for first-time buyers; the response's 10-year windows for new and existing loans misstate the reform.
Maintenance deduction ends with the reform rather than becoming capped lump sums.
summary: Response correctly says nothing changes this year and covers ending deductions, but states the wrong in-force date (2028 vs 2029) as certain, gives directive amortisation advice, and directs to the bank rather than tax authorities.
